Show connectors

The 3→4 connector is activated in this module. The informational 4→5 and 5→6 connectors are activated with the four buttons in the header, according to the ball direction (R to L or L to R). These connectors do not affect the calculation of the aiming point.

Cue ball and systemBlanca · LKL / Base 50⌄

The app uses the white ball as the cue ball by default. If yellow is selected, all calculations use yellow as the cue ball.

LKL / Base 50 is intended for routes of up to three cushions. Plus is intended for short → long → long patterns, with the third long cushion serving as the zero cushion.

Position the balls by measuring distances to the cushionsManual entry in centimetres⌄

Drag the balls or enter their distances in centimetres. Use a decimal point or comma. The ball moves as you type. Playing surface: 284 × 142 cm cushion to cushion. Visual frame: 5 cm blue cushion and 9 cm brown rail. Start and aiming point are projected to the diamond centreline; arrival is marked on the cushion nose.

Position from photo or overhead cameraOverhead camera or image file⌄

Capture the table directly with an overhead camera or upload a photo. The app will attempt to detect the corners and balls automatically; any point can then be corrected with the loupe and fine adjustment. The 284 × 142 cm playing surface will be defined by the four confirmed corner points.

Use this function only if you have an overhead camera installed. Otherwise, upload a photo file in the field below.
The app opens the camera once in stable 1920 × 1080 mode, waits 3 seconds for focus, and sends the image directly to the detector.
or upload a photo
From the right short cushion: the table’s upper-left corner corresponds to the photo’s upper-right corner.
Recommendation: first choose the side from which the photo was taken. Automatic detection proposes initial points and offsets the corners 5 cm inward; the final playing surface is defined by the four confirmed points.
Train from YouTube and other sourcesCapture positions from videos, PDFs or images⌄

The purple title of this section is the button: tap it and the app goes straight to capture (this arrow ⌄ only opens this help). The ritual: open the overhead view in another Chrome tab or in any window (YouTube or Kozoom paused, a PDF in Acrobat, an image in Photos) and leave it in view on the position you want to steal; tap the purple title; Chrome will ask you to pick that tab or window (once per session). On the captured frame, the first time you will mark the four corners of the cloth (they are saved; use "Recalibrate corners" if you changed video or framing) and then three clicks: white, yellow and red. The balls land on the virtual table, ready for training. Fine print: windows must be restored, not minimized; if a Store app does not appear in the picker, open the file in a Chrome tab.

No capture yet.
With voice enabled, say «record» from any section to open the recording module. The control at the bottom shows when the app is listening and lets you turn voice off. Inside the module, say «record in five, ten or fifteen», «stop and review», «replay», «record» to prepare another recording, or «download with data», as appropriate. Say «capture table» from any section to take a photograph and review the positions. The capture reuses the session’s corners when applicable; check the balls and click «Apply positions to the app». «Put the balls back» retrieves the last confirmed position from any section, even when the purple button is hidden. This position is retained when you leave practice and is replaced when you apply another. If a capture, recording or export is in progress, the request waits until it finishes. Opening the module does not start recording automatically. Voice uses Chrome’s speech service (internet required) and the default Windows microphone: select the Logitech Brio there. When the recording module is ready, you can also simply say «five», «ten» or «fifteen».

From 5 to 120 seconds, with an automatic half-second pause. The next listening window starts when listening is confirmed. A command that has just started gets a short grace period to finish. Muting manually stops the cycle. The interval is saved in this browser.

Voice command history

Keeps up to 1000 entries for speech, transcripts and actions, plus the last 200 connection status entries, only while this page is open; no audio is saved. Includes provisional transcripts and speech detection, with millisecond timestamps. The session and result reference lets you follow the same command. Click «Refresh» to see the latest entries.

Shot sequenceBall first · upper long → right short⌄

For free shots not played with LKL / Base 50 or Plus: no trajectories or aiming points; the recording will show only the ball circles. It turns off when any sequence is chosen.

The slider sets your table's maximum lengthening, applied in full on shallow rebounds; on steep ones (more than ~52° against the cushion) the engine reduces it by itself, down to the pure mirror near 70°, following the curve measured on the table. It ships tuned for a typical table (1.25); if your balls arrive consistently long or short of the line, move it until they match and it will be saved.

The five-shot ritual. Cue ball on the L2 line, about a hand’s width (some 25 cm) off the bottom cushion; level cue, tip just above centre, natural roll with zero sidespin, medium and even speed. Shoot each shot at least twice, until the arrival settles, and note where the ball touched the second cushion: C is counted on the right short cushion from the top (upper corner = C0) and L on the lower long cushion from left to right. If you have the overhead camera, record each shot and read the arrival on the video.

Double-click (or double-tap) the chart to enlarge it; double-click again, the Esc key, or the Close button returns it to size.

T5 is the control shot: it must arrive at L4.00 on any table. If it strays more than ±0.15, the assistant issues no verdict; repeat it before trusting the session.

Geometric mirror system. Base: rolling ball (center or half a tip above), zero sidespin, natural rolling speed. Sidespin takes no part in the calculation.

The base is the separation, in spaces (diamonds), at which the ¼-ball angle is neutral on your table: with ball 3 on ball 2's line and the cue ball at that distance, the shot scores with spin 0. The author sets it at 2.0. Calibration ritual: set up the spin-0 position and play it several times with the system's contract; if your shots come up consistently short, raise the base; if they run long, lower it. The value is saved and is independent of the Mirror coefficient.

Pasones system: up-and-back three-cushion shots between the long cushions. Fixed contract: ¼ ball, follow-through stroke letting the cue go, medium-high speed. The system's only output is the spin.

The arrival is read on the remaining ball, and the diagnostics name it.

The adjustment is added to the calculated spin, to fit the system to your table and style: if your renversés come up consistently short, raise it; if they run long, lower it. Default is 0 and the value is saved.

Renversé system: the cue ball always attacks the corner in projection (the first diamond of the long cushion at the corner, not the corner point), with reverse spin, follow-through stroke and no excess speed. Spin = start + arrival, and the app always calls it in whole numbers.

Choose whether the shot starts ball-first or cushion-first, then set the cushion sequence.

Shot video with overlaid dataOverhead camera · not calibrated⌄

Record the real execution with the overhead camera and review it with the shot data (Target point and line, and Arrival point) overlaid on the video, with slow motion and frame-by-frame advance. The recording includes the camera microphone's audio. It requires calibrating the four table corners once, as long as the camera does not move. If you apply positions from an overhead capture of the automatic detector, that calibration is reused automatically.

The overlaid data (Target and Arrival) will be whatever is calculated at that moment (for example, LKL / Base 50 with the chosen cue ball and cushion sequence).

Four-corner calibration

Drag each point to the inner corner of the cloth (where the cushions meet), in this order as the table appears in the app: 1 upper left, 2 upper right, 3 lower right, 4 lower left. Green points 5 and 6 go on the cloth edge, at the center of the upper long cushion and the right short cushion: with them the app measures the lens curvature so it can straighten it. The ball rings and the projected diamonds must match the video. Fine adjustment: keyboard arrows (with Shift, 5-pixel steps) or the buttons below.

Position from photo: the app proposes corners offset 5 cm inward and ball centers. If detection is not perfect, select the corresponding point, correct it with the loupe and confirm. The orientation is taken from the previous selector: right short cushion, left short cushion, lower long cushion or upper long cushion.

Roger Conti's sidespin

This app uses the sidespin scale described by Roger Conti, as shown in the image. Each spin step is a half-ferrule lateral offset (6 mm if the cue tip measures 12 mm). Using “cascade” or “clock-style” spin may yield slightly different results.
